pos.personaBrief: Bielsismo is defined by pressing and vertical speed, with possession a means (La Nacion: attacks backed by seven players, quick cutback), not an end; Chile's possession game under Sampaoli is a variation.

pro.personaBrief: Fast transitions with six men running beyond the ball (Hardtackle), 7 players in the box and quick cutbacks (La Nacion), yet build-up from the back against the press (Spielverlagerung, TGG Medel 2v1).

est.personaBrief: Movement, rotation and interplay in congested areas (TGG, FFT) point to relational play, but a rehearsed mother system with defined shapes (24horas, FFT) and wide fullbacks keep structure.

lar.personaBrief: Wide forwards and high wide fullbacks stretch laterally, overloading wings (Spielverlagerung, FFT, SBS), and the 3-3-1-3 relies on wide forwards.

blo.personaBrief: Defending in the opponent's half, immediate counterpressing with six or seven men and forwards pressing centre-backs (Grantland, Spielverlagerung, Hardtackle).

mar.personaBrief: Man-marking all over the pitch with a free safety, and man-to-man at set pieces with clear individual responsibility (Grantland, La Nacion).

pla.personaBrief: Bielsa does not cede his ideas, rejects alternative plans and not building philosophy around players (FFT, 2017 quote), prefers to die with his style (La Nacion), though he studies opponents extensively.

res.personaBrief: Never makes defensive changes to protect a result, prefers to die with his own style (La Nacion), constant pressing and not thinking about defending (24horas).

sis.personaBrief: System over stars: heavy tactical repetition, everyone runs and presses (Grantland, FFT), roles converted by the model such as Medel and Javi Martinez.

jog.personaBrief: Running is commitment; physically brutal intensity and hybrid players redeployed (Grantland, TGG), little space for a non-running 10 (Bielsa's enganche aside).

bas.personaBrief: Newell's scouted young players, Chile 2007-10 generation, Leeds with fewer than 20 seniors and academy fill-ins (FourFourTwo, SBS).

lid.personaBrief: Bielsa keeps distance, runs players into the ground and demands equal rules and homework; he is the boss with an extremist stance (FFT).
